observations.description: Battery cell 3 drifts outside the normal balancing band.
Battery cell 3 internal resistance rises and terminal voltage begins an unexpected decline under load.
Battery terminal voltage crosses the 26.2 V warning threshold.
EPS sheds 85 W of non-essential load to protect the main bus.
Battery heater power is cut from 18 W to 8 W during load shedding.
Available power falls below the mission-operations allocation.
Reduced heater and pump power let the thermal loop drift above its setpoint.
Reduced reaction-wheel torque authority pushes attitude error past 0.5 deg.
Transmitter power is reduced from 10.5 W to 7.4 W to preserve the bus.
Flight computer CPU load exceeds 75% while managing the power shortfall.
A marginal bus triggers a flight computer watchdog reset.
The onboard computer enters safe mode and sheds payload and non-essential loads.
Downlink rate falls to 64 kbps and signal-to-noise ratio approaches the critical threshold.
Battery terminal voltage crosses the 24.8 V critical threshold.
Battery temperature crosses the 32 degC warning threshold.
Mission operations declare a mission-level failure because payload downlink cannot be recovered in safe mode.
Safe mode stabilizes at a reduced power state with the battery above its state-of-charge critical limit.

hypotheses.title: EPS battery cell imbalance cascade
hypotheses.summary: Battery cell imbalance caused voltage sag, triggering load shedding and reduced power that propagated failures across subsystems.
assumptions: The observed events accurately reflect the underlying physical state
Load shedding directly reduces power available to all downstream subsystems
REJECTED: contradicted by 3 evidence; 10 unsupported links

hypotheses.title: Comms antenna temperature telemetry fault
hypotheses.summary: A spurious antenna temperature spike in telemetry caused the thermal control system to shed heater power, reducing power availability and degrading communications.
assumptions: The antenna temperature reading is erroneous (sensor/telemetry fault)
Thermal control reacts to the faulty temperature by shedding heater power
REJECTED: contradicted by 3 evidence; 5 unsupported links

hypotheses.title: OBC CPU overload leading to safe mode
hypotheses.summary: Excessive CPU load on the OBC triggered watchdog resets and forced entry into safe mode, halting mission operations.
assumptions: High CPU load directly causes watchdog resets
Safe‑mode entry follows a watchdog reset
REJECTED: contradicted by 2 evidence; 6 unsupported links

hypotheses.title: ADCS gyro bias drift causing attitude degradation
hypotheses.summary: Drift in ADCS gyro bias increased attitude error and reduced star‑tracker confidence, leading to an attitude‑control degradation event.
assumptions: Gyro bias drift is the primary driver of the observed attitude error
Star‑tracker confidence drops as a consequence of increased attitude error
REJECTED: contradicted by 3 evidence; 4 unsupported links
